column2: How do I see my censuses as a grid, draw a proof file, a word tree of records, parish areas or a star map?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, group “My research”: 🗓️ Census grid (one row per person, one cell per census from 1836 to 1936: found, not found, to search, not yet born, already dead, outside France; “Worklist to print” form; a click on a cell opens the person page), ⚖️ Proof diagram (the question, the clues for and against with their weight, the searches and conflicts, the conclusion and its certainty, top to bottom or left to right; a hypothesis to compare gives one column per answer) and 🌿 Word tree of records (what follows or precedes “fils de”, “veuve de”… in your transcriptions). Group “Maps”: Choropleth map → Level of detail “Parishes” (an area around each church, from the pre-1790 parishes of your places) and Migration map → “From the app” → “✳️ All the links of a place” (incoming spouses, children who left, emigrants) or the “Star map” setting. Map → 🧭 Tools → Distances and travel times → “⭕ In one day”: the circles reached on foot, on horseback, by stagecoach or by train depending on the year, and your family’s places inside them. For each one, “From the app” takes the group of people (ancestors, branch, label, list…), the period and the “＋ Criterion” rules; the table in the Data tab stays yours: add, remove or correct a row, change a colour, paste a table or a CSV; nothing is overwritten until you ask “From the app” again.
